hints: Look at the functional group in each formula first, and match each test to the group it is famous for detecting.
Notice that $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ contains a $\text{C=C}$ double bond, while $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ contains an aldehyde $\text{-CHO}$ group.
Link $\text{C=C}$ to electrophilic addition with bromine, and link aldehyde (but not ketone) to oxidation by Tollens reagent, then find the row that pairs them correctly.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three functional groups**

Great start, let's name what we have. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone. $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is an alkene alcohol, it has both $\text{C=C}$ and $\text{-OH}$.

**Who decolourises bromine water?**

Remember, orange bromine water is decolourised by $\text{C=C}$ in an electrophilic addition reaction. Only the alkene alcohol can do this.

$$\text{CH}_2\text{=CH- + Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Br-CHBr-}$$

**Who gives a silver mirror with Tollens reagent?**

Tollens reagent, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+$, is a mild oxidising agent. It oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, forming silver metal, but it cannot oxidise ketones.

$$\text{RCHO + 2[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + 2\text{Ag + 4NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Match to the table**

So decolourises bromine water is $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Forms a silver mirror is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$. That combination is the correct row.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde with no $\text{C=C}$, so it does not decolourise bromine water. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone, so it is not oxidised by Tollens reagent and gives no silver mirror.
options.B: Half right, half wrong. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ correctly gives a silver mirror as an aldehyde, but $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone with no $\text{C=C}$ and does not decolourise bromine water.
options.C: Half right, half wrong. $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ correctly decolourises bromine water because of its alkene group, but $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone and gives a negative Tollens test.
options.D: Correct and well done. The alkene $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ decolourises bromine water by addition across $\text{C=C}$. The aldehyde $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is oxidised by Tollens reagent to give the silver mirror, while the ketone does neither.
